body.statement:
The supremum of \(\operatorname{OPT}(G,s,c)/\operatorname{LP}(G,s,c)\)
over unit-cost bow-free singleton instances with \(r(G,s)\leq3\),
\(\mathcal C(G,s)\neq\varnothing\), and radius-two bidirected trees equals
two. For \(G_{K_n}\) with \(n\geq2\), the ratio is \(2-2/n\). Under
\(\mathsf{UGC}\), for every fixed \(\epsilon>0\), no polynomial-time
\((2-\epsilon)\)-approximation exists on this same promised-rank class.
body.justification: A matching gap family and conditional lower bound certify that factor two is the exact polynomial frontier under the standard conjecture.
body.gap: Khot and Regev establish the threshold for vertex cover, and Singh characterizes the source LP gap; no published result transfers the threshold to a bounded-rank causal-effect-identification design class.
body.consumer: Algorithm designers can treat a certified factor-two rank-three solution as worst-case optimal under \(\mathsf{UGC}\), focusing engineering effort on instance-specific improvement.
body.proof_tex:
We prove the narrowed, well-typed statement, restricting the ratio to
instances with \(\mathcal C(G,s)\neq\varnothing\).  On such a unit-cost
instance, any \(R\in\mathcal C(G,s)\) gives
\[
 \sum_{v\in V^{-}}y_v\geq\sum_{v\in R}y_v\geq1
\]
for every LP-feasible \(y\); hence \(\operatorname{LP}(G,s,c)>0\), so the
ratio is defined.  Theorem \(\mathrm{thm{:}rank\mbox{-}three\mbox{-}rounding}\)
then gives
\[
 \frac{\operatorname{OPT}(G,s,c)}{\operatorname{LP}(G,s,c)}\leq2.
\]

For the matching sequence, take \(H=K_n\) with \(n\geq2\) and its
private-guard expansion.  Theorems
\(\mathrm{thm{:}private\mbox{-}guard\mbox{-}realization}\) and
\(\mathrm{thm{:}objective\mbox{-}preserving\mbox{-}hardness}\) give the
required bow-free, rank-three, radius-two structure and
\[
 \operatorname{OPT}(G_{K_n},s,c)=\tau(K_n)=n-1.
\]
The fractional vector \(y_{x_u}=1/2\) and \(y_{z_e}=0\) is feasible for
every residual triple, so its objective is \(n/2\).  Conversely, summing all
\(\binom n2\) residual constraints and dividing by \(n-1\) gives, for every
feasible \(y\),
\[
 \sum_{u\in U}y_{x_u}
 +\frac1{n-1}\sum_{e\in E}y_{z_e}
 \geq\frac{\binom n2}{n-1}=\frac n2.
\]
Since \(n\geq2\), the unit-cost objective is at least the left side.  Thus
\(\operatorname{LP}(G_{K_n},s,c)=n/2\) and
\[
 \frac{\operatorname{OPT}(G_{K_n},s,c)}
 {\operatorname{LP}(G_{K_n},s,c)}
 =\frac{n-1}{n/2}=2-\frac2n.
\]
Together with the upper bound, this proves that the supremum is two.

For conditional hardness, suppose for some fixed \(\epsilon>0\) that a
polynomial algorithm achieved factor \(2-\epsilon\) on the stated causal
class.  Given any source graph \(H\) with at least one edge, construct
\(G_H\), run that algorithm, and replace every selected guard by an endpoint
as in the proof of Theorem
\(\mathrm{thm{:}objective\mbox{-}preserving\mbox{-}hardness}\).  The
resulting vertex cover \(C_A\) satisfies
\[
 |C_A|\leq |A|
 \leq(2-\epsilon)\operatorname{OPT}(G_H,s,c)
 =(2-\epsilon)\tau(H).
\]
All transformations are polynomial, and edgeless source instances are
trivial.  This contradicts the cited Lemma
\(\mathrm{lem{:}ugc\mbox{-}vertex\mbox{-}cover\mbox{-}hardness}\) under
\(\mathsf{UGC}\).  Hence no such causal approximation algorithm exists.
